Y2 is primarily driven by X3 (negative), X4 (negative), and X6 (positive), with X2 slightly positive. There is a key trade-off: X2 and X4 increase both Y1 and Y4 but also increase Y2; X3 strongly helps Y3 constraint and reduces Y2 but only moderately helps Y1. X6 increases Y2 (bad) and decreases Y4 (bad) but can increase Y1 in some regimes. The X4×X6 interaction is weak — effects are largely additive.

new_findings: X5 has a threshold/saturation effect on Y1: Y1 jumps ~0.30 as X5 goes from 0.1 to 0.5, then saturates. No effect on Y2, Y3, Y4.
X2 has a convex (accelerating) effect on Y1 — gradient increases from 0.02 at low to 0.95 at high. Also increases Y4 linearly (~0.17 range) and Y2 slightly (~0.08 range). Zero effect on Y3.
X4 and X6 interact very weakly (interaction std ~0.015 for Y1, ~0.014 for Y2) despite each having strong individual main effects. Their effects are additive.
X7-X12 have exactly zero local gradients at 5 different tested points spanning the input space. They are truly inert inputs.
Y3 is controlled exclusively by X1 and X3 — no other input affects it. X3 is the dominant driver (gradient 0.31-0.61).
X3 has zero gradient for Y4 at all tested points despite correlation of 0.60 — this correlation was confounded by covariance with X2/X4 in the initial dataset.
X4's gradient for Y2 is highly nonlinear: ranges from -1.23 at low settings to +0.09 at high settings. X6 shows similar regime-dependent behavior on Y2.
surprises: X5 was predicted to have no effect (zero gradients at center and extremes), but OAT sweep revealed a strong threshold effect on Y1 (range=0.30) active only in the lower half of its range. The gradients missed this because all test points were in the saturated region.

X4×X6 interaction was predicted to be strong based on dramatically different gradients at different points, but the factorial test showed weak interaction (std=0.015). The gradient changes were due to individual nonlinearities, not coupled interaction.
X3->Y4 correlation of 0.60 turned out to be entirely spurious — gradient is exactly zero at every tested point. This was a confounding artifact in the 24-point observational dataset.

Run OAT sweep on X1 to understand its nonlinear effect on Y3 (gradient drops from 0.51 to 0.02 at high values). 3. Begin optimization: evaluate candidate Pareto-optimal points using knowledge of causal structure — high X3 for Y3 constraint, high X2+X4 for Y1+Y4, low X6 for Y2, X5≥0.5 for Y1 threshold. 4. Test whether X6 should be low (helps Y2, Y4) or moderate (helps Y1) at different trade-off points.
